question: Can variational inference over continuous quantities be reformulated as tractable inference over their finite bitstring representations, including quantized neural-network weights?

key_findings.claim: BitVI represents a continuous variational family through a deterministic probabilistic circuit over number-system bits.
key_findings.evidence: A fixed-point mapping sends circuit-sampled bitstrings to real values; tractable circuit entropy supplies the ELBO entropy term and an inverse tree-CDF plus straight-through estimator supplies samples and gradients.

key_findings.claim: Very low precision can capture the tested non-Gaussian two-dimensional densities better than a single full-covariance Gaussian family.
key_findings.evidence: Four- and eight-bit circuits reproduce multimodality and curved dependence in Gaussian-mixture, ring, funnel, and banana targets; the visual comparison shows where full-covariance Gaussian VI cannot express these shapes.

key_findings.claim: On small Bayesian neural-network benchmarks, BitVI is usually statistically comparable to Gaussian VI even at four or eight bits.
key_findings.evidence: Across 25 small-data binary classification tasks and five-fold cross-validation, Table 1 reports negative log predictive density; paired tests find BitVI not significantly different from mean-field or full-covariance Gaussian VI on most tasks, though it is not uniformly best.

key_findings.claim: Model width matters more than extra bit depth in the two-moons ablation after a modest precision threshold.
key_findings.evidence: Sweeping two to twelve bits and hidden-layer widths from four to sixteen units shows NLPD improves more consistently with network size, while four- and eight-bit variants often saturate; accuracy and calibration appendices show the same broad pattern.

method.core_idea: Optimize an ELBO whose variational distribution is a probabilistic circuit over the bits of a fixed-point representation rather than a continuous Gaussian parameterization.
method.mechanism: Alternating bit decisions form a tree-structured circuit, exact circuit entropy is computed recursively, inverse-CDF traversal samples bitstrings, and a straight-through estimator passes gradients through the discrete number mapping.
assumptions: The target density can be evaluated up to its normalization constant.
The selected finite number range and precision cover posterior mass adequately.
Mean-field factorization across high-dimensional neural weights is acceptable for scalable experiments.

techniques.role: Turns numerical precision choices into the support and hierarchy of the approximate posterior.
Provides expressive discrete dependencies with tractable entropy and sampling.
Approximates gradients through the non-differentiable fixed-point decode.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic non-Gaussian one- and two-dimensional densities
evaluations.metric: Density fit and qualitative mass coverage
evaluations.result: Four bits capture the broad shapes and eight bits visually approach saturation on several targets.

evaluations.metric: Negative log predictive density with five-fold cross-validation
evaluations.result: Four- and eight-bit BitVI are statistically comparable to Gaussian baselines on most datasets.
evaluations.baseline: Mean-field Gaussian VI and full-covariance Gaussian VI

evaluations.setting: Two-moons neural networks over width and 2-12 bit depth
evaluations.metric: NLPD, accuracy, and expected calibration error
evaluations.result: Increasing hidden units dominates increasing precision across much of the grid.

limitations: High-dimensional experiments restore a mean-field posterior because a fully dependent bit tree is too costly.
The circuit introduces many optimized parameters and the paper does not demonstrate large modern networks or hardware speedups.
Experiments use fixed-point representations; floating-point exponent structure remains untested.
failure_modes: Posterior mass outside the chosen fixed-point range is clipped or unreachable.
Reverse-KL training can still omit modes even when the circuit family can represent them.
Straight-through gradients may bias optimization, especially near bit-boundary changes.
reusable_insights: Numerical representation is itself a structured probabilistic modeling choice, not only an implementation detail.
Precision-depth ablations should be crossed with model-capacity ablations because extra bits and extra parameters solve different bottlenecks.
Tractable circuit entropy can make discrete variational families practical when sampling-based entropy estimates are unstable.
open_questions: Can structured sparse circuits retain cross-weight dependence at transformer scale?
Does BitVI deliver measured memory, latency, or energy gains on low-precision hardware after circuit overhead?
How should exponent and mantissa bits be allocated adaptively for floating-point posteriors?

competitive_landscape.title: Bit Blasting Probabilistic Programs
competitive_landscape.difference: HyBit discretizes hybrid probabilistic programs into Boolean inference problems; BitVI learns a variational posterior over parameter bitstrings with circuit entropy and gradient optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: Probabilistic Circuits for Variational Inference in Discrete Graphical Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Shih and Ermon compute exact ELBOs for discrete graphical models under selective circuits; BitVI uses circuits to induce approximate distributions over decoded continuous values and neural weights.

competitive_landscape.title: Weight Uncertainty in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Bayes by Backprop optimizes continuous factorized weight distributions, while BitVI places the variational mass directly on quantized weight bitstrings.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: discrete probabilistic circuits and bit-blasted inference both predate this work. The new combination is to treat a numeric bitstring code as the variational family for continuous and neural-weight inference, with tractable circuit entropy and explicit precision-capacity studies.
reviewer_notes: The full UAI manuscript, appendices, table settings, and author-stated limitations were checked. The paper demonstrates statistical fidelity, not end-to-end systems efficiency. Primary competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
